title: Debris
summary: Automatic cleanup: Debris:AddItem(instance, lifetime) destroys the instance after the given seconds — the standard way to expire effects, projectiles, and clones without manual timers.

methods.name: AddItem
methods.description: Destroys the instance after `lifetime` seconds (default 10). Re-adding an item updates its timer.

methods.name: SetMaxItems
methods.description: Caps how many items Debris tracks (default 1000); excess oldest items are destroyed immediately.

explanation.whatItIs: A janitor with a stopwatch. Hand it any instance and a lifetime; it destroys it for you when time's up.
explanation.whyItExists: Temporary objects (explosions, bullet casings, clone effects) pile up fast; forgetting to destroy them leaks memory and instances forever.
whenToUse: Visual effects and particles spawned at runtime
Anywhere you'd write `task.delay(n, function() part:Destroy() end)`
whenNotToUse: For objects that might still be needed — Debris destroys unconditionally
When you need conditional cleanup — write your own logic
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
Debris:AddItem(effect, 3)
   │
   └── 3 seconds later → effect:Destroy() happens automatically
```
No task.delay, no bookkeeping, no forgotten clones.
tips: Pair with :Clone() spawners: clone, parent, AddItem — three lines, zero leaks
Re-AddItem the same instance to refresh its expiry
commonMistakes: Adding an instance that gameplay still references (it WILL vanish)
Assuming Debris runs client-side for server-created parts — destruction happens where the instance lives

examples.title: Self-cleaning projectile
examples.code:
local Debris = game:GetService("Debris")

local function shootBullet(origin: Vector3, direction: Vector3)
    local bullet = Instance.new("Part")
    bullet.Size = Vector3.new(0.5, 0.5, 1)
    bullet.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(origin, origin + direction)
    bullet.Parent = workspace
    bullet.AssemblyLinearVelocity = direction * 150

    Debris:AddItem(bullet, 4)   -- gone after 4s no matter what
end
